subject: Clarification: hosted API deletion orchestration, SLA, and evidence pack
messages:
From: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Data deletion assurance + evidence for hosted API

Hi Karthik,

We are updating our security questionnaire and need clear, itemized answers regarding data deletion for the Redwood hosted API. Specifically:

1) On tenant-initiated deletion (via support ticket or API), what is the SLA to remove customer-owned data from: live inference stores, persistent logs, and backups/archives?
2) What exact artifacts do you provide as evidence that deletion occurred (audit logs, S3 object delete manifests, timestamped ticket IDs)?
3) Are there differences in the process when data was used to build ephemeral caches / KV stores or embeddings?
4) Can data be restricted to a US region (we prefer us-west-2) and will that change deletion timelines?

Our compliance team needs written responses and an example evidence package by June 30 to include with the audit. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Laura Cheng
Security Manager, Acme Health
laura.cheng@acmehealth.com
+1 415 555 0123
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data deletion assurance + evidence for hosted API

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, below I map each ask to the actionable item and evidence we can provide.

TL;DR
- Live inference data and customer prompt/output blobs: removed from serving layer within 1 business day; primary object store deletion completed within 24 hours of request.
- Operational logs (indexing/observability): retained for 7 days by default, can be reduced under enterprise agreement; backups/archived snapshots: scrubbed on a 90-day cycle with a certified scrub and tracked deletion job.
- Embeddings and KV caches: eviction from runtime is immediate; persistent embedding indices are removed as part of the primary delete flow (24 hours).
- Region pinning: yes — we support region-scoped tenancy (us-west-2). Deletion SLAs apply the same; evidence shows region origin of objects.

What we will provide (example evidence pack attached):
- A redwood deletion ticket ID with timestamp and originating user/tenant ID.
- Object deletion manifest: list of object keys removed and delete markers (S3-style) with timestamps and region tags.
- Audit log excerpt showing orchestration steps (tenant flagging -> purge job -> confirmation).
- Hash/checksum record for scrubbed snapshots and a signed statement from our security team.

Im attaching a short playbook and an example evidence template; Kimberly (security) and Priyom (ops) are looped for technical details. Let us know if the auditor needs a specific format.

Next steps:
1) I will have Kimberly send the technical deletion flow and a sample evidence pack by EOD tomorrow.
2) We can open a dedicated support ticket that will act as the authoritative deletion request (and we will provide the ticket ID for your records).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data deletion assurance + evidence for hosted API

Laura / Karthik — putting the technical playbook in writing here so you have a single source of truth. I attached the full PDF (redwood-erase-playbook-v1.pdf) but key points below.

Deletion orchestration (hosted API)
1) Request intake: customer deletes via Support portal (ticket API) or by emailing support@redwoodinference.com. Ticket is assigned and tenant flag "pending_erase" is set (immutable audit entry).
2) Immediate serving purge: any in-memory or ephemeral KV caches are marked and evicted within minutes. This prevents future access to that data from the runtime.
3) Primary object store deletion: a purge job runs against the tenant's objects in our primary blob store (S3-like) and issues delete markers. This job completes within 24 hours; the job emits a manifest file that lists removed keys and timestamps.
4) Observability/logs: application-level logs that contain user payloads are rotated; by default we retain those indices for 7 days. If you require shorter retention we will adjust retention policies under contract.
5) Backups & snapshots: incremental backups are subject to our archival retention. We run a 90-day scrub window for archived snapshots; when a tenant requests erasure we mark snapshots for prioritized scrubbing — actual physical unlinking may take up to 90 days. All scrub operations are recorded and a signed manifest is produced.

Embeddings and derived artifacts
- Embeddings stored in persistent vector indices are treated as tenant-owned artifacts and are deleted as part of the primary object store purge. Runtime caches are evicted immediately.

Evidence artifacts we provide
- deletion_ticket_id: the support ticket ID with the initiating user and timestamp.
- delete_manifest.csv: list of object keys and delete markers (region-tagged).
- purge_job_log.txt: stdout/stderr of the purge orchestration with job id and run timestamps.
- scrub_certificate.pdf: signed certificate when backups/snapshots are scrubbed.
- sha256-hashes.txt: optional checksum list for scrubbed objects.

Example timeline (typical):
- Day 0: customer files request -> immediate runtime eviction -> ticket created.
- Day 1: primary object store purge completes and we provide delete_manifest.csv.
- Days 2-7: observability indices rotate and become inaccessible; short-term logs expire per retention policy.
- Day 1-90: archived snapshot scrub priority; we provide scrub_certificate once completed.

Region pinning
- When you request region pinning (us-west-2), tenant objects are provisioned in that region and manifests include region metadata. Our deletion flows work the same; proof includes region tags in the manifest and S3-style delete markers.

If you want, we can produce a one-page attestation letter and a sample evidence package formatted for your auditor.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
From: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data deletion assurance + evidence for hosted API

Thanks Karthik/Kimberly — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications so we can sign off with audit: 

- Can you confirm the default observability/log retention (7 days) is not accessible to product teams or engineers after eviction? We need assurance those logs cannot be reconstructed or used for training.
- For the 90-day scrub window on archives, can you provide an SLA option (for enterprise customers) to accelerate scrub to 30 days?

Auditor wants an example evidence pack in our preferred format (CSV manifests + signed PDF cert). If you can attach one sample and a short attestation letter, that would be ideal. Deadline remains June 30.

Laura
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data deletion assurance + evidence for hosted API

Laura — brief answers and next steps.

1) Observability indices: once the tenant is flagged and purge runs, indices containing customer payloads are logically sealed and access is removed from all non-audit roles. Engineers do not have ad-hoc access to the sealed indices. For auditors we provide exports (redacted or full) via the evidence pack. We will include a signed attestation that logs are not used for training.

2) Accelerated scrub SLA: yes — we offer an Enterprise add-on to reduce the archive scrub window to 30 days. This is a contract-level option (we can include in an addendum).

Attached: sample evidence pack (acme-evidence-template.zip) and a draft one-page attestation.

Mutual action plan:
- Today: we open a deletion ticket once you confirm the tenant id (please reply with your tenant id or let us open from support).
- +1 day: primary purge manifest and purge_job_log provided.
- +30 days: if you choose accelerated scrub SLA, provide scrub_certificate within 30 days; otherwise scrub completion and certificate within 90 days.

If that timeline works, I will have support auto-generate the ticket and Kimberly will deliver the attestation PDF.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: redwood-erase-playbook-v1.pdf, acme-evidence-template.zip, soc2-summary-2025.pdf
